result.topic_en: Riemann discusses branch points (Verzweigungspunkte) of an algebraic function s defined by F(s,z)=0, where two or more values of s coincide; he relates their number to the discriminant-type product of F'(s_i) and expands F near a point where F = dF/ds = 0.

methods.what: Branch points occur where F(s,z)=0 has coinciding roots, i.e. where F'(s)=0 simultaneously
Discriminant-type polynomial Q(z) whose roots give branch points; degree 2m(n-1)
Taylor expansion of F about a point (alpha,beta) on the curve
At a simple branch point s-alpha behaves like (z-beta)^{1/2}
Number of simple branch points equals 2m(n-1)
